text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The killer of industrialist Ozdemir Sabanci surrenders to the Turkish embassy in Damascus.
- Up to 150,000 workers protest on the streets of Ankara for more democracy and improved labour conditions.
- The finance minister promises to give additional salary rises to state employees.
- The cross-border military operation into northern Iraq is complete with 160 guerrillas from the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) having been killed.
- Three members of a special anti-terror team will give statements to a parliamentary commission about a car crash which pointed to links between underworld gangs and the state.
- Iran is a mediator in Turkish-Syrian relations. Iranian Foreign Minister Velayati says Turkey welcomes Tehran's mediation proposal.
- The fiasco of eleven years of privatization: since 1985 when Turkey began implementing privatisation only $3.1 billion worth of sales have been carried out.
- Bankers believe repos will be a very attractive investment in 1997.
